<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-bundle-members.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via getMetaItemLayered (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-bundle-members.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1950f075460dfcda4dd7602c5c71e21385f37ed8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6c4433fb7326eeeac64a6c521c38834bbf4bc422` — the merge of head `e90a02e17bd8440eb2fd23020c757837afb867c9` into base `1950f075460dfcda4dd7602c5c71e21385f37ed8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6c4433fb7326eeeac64a6c521c38834bbf4bc422 && git checkout 6c4433fb7326eeeac64a6c521c38834bbf4bc422
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1950f075460dfcda4dd7602c5c71e21385f37ed8 e90a02e17bd8440eb2fd23020c757837afb867c9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1950f075460dfcda4dd7602c5c71e21385f37ed8 && git merge --no-ff e90a02e17bd8440eb2fd23020c757837afb867c9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1950f075460dfcda4dd7602c5c71e21385f37ed8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1950f075460dfcda4dd7602c5c71e21385f37ed8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L2 round on head 90b5cdeb4f: S1 and S2 sent back, seat ruling on S1 · 2026-11-17T22:56Z

The seat's at-tier reviewer sub-agent read this head and found no must-fix and two should-fix. Its record is NOT posted as the record of this head: its transcript holds a synthetic usage-limit turn, which `verify-review-tier.mjs` refuses. The fresh at-tier record is rendered on the fixed head.

**S1 (should-fix): the holder's first member still reaches both reads at an exact address.** `readMetaItem` and `getMetaItemLayered` end an exact address in `exactQualifierItem(…, member)` (`protocol-exact-qualifier.ts`). When the item in hand is another package's, it is replaced by `registry.getPackageScopedItem(type, name, holder, member)` with the raw selector. Naming no member, that answers canonical-first, else the holder's first member. So, read from the tree and not run, at an exact address the read naming no member still differs from `?member=en-US` whenever another package holds the canonical member. The base-address mirror and the re-addressed read move with it. `packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts` asserts the old answer on purpose.

**Seat ruling on S1: exit (a).**
Ruling-ref: the governing text is the selector sentence in `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (~399-403): "Absent, the canonical member … which is what a bare-name read answers; naming the canonical value is the same request … a well-formed member with nothing stored or shipped answers as that door answers an absent item."
SKILL.md: spec and code disagree ⇒ align the code. This is the card's own defect at a third site, not a new product decision; the pin that asserts the old answer asserts the departure from that sentence, so it flips.
- Hold the replacement to the addressed member in both reads.
- Flip that pin's last leg.
- Pin the base-address mirror (naming no member equals naming `en-US`, at the address and through the re-address).
- Name the exact address in the ledger entry.

**S2 (should-fix): the ledger entry names less than the diff moves.** `18.bundle-without-canonical-member-bare-read-absent.ts` quantifies over a name "that no layer ships or stores in its canonical member", but the diff also moves the read naming no member where a dependent stores the canonical member over a base that ships only another one. The sibling `18.shipped-base-dependent-canonical-row-not-published.ts` (unshipped, same step) ends "The plain read, ?member=CANONICAL and the execution read do not move", which is now false. Fix: name the arrangement in the new entry, and correct the sibling's last sentence.

**Pending changeset correction.** `.changeset/34441-shipped-base-canonical-member-one-answer.md` (pending on `main`) states two answers this PR reverses (`/layers` naming no member "TO A's `fr-FR` (200)", and the plain read under "Not moved"). It is amended in this PR as a DELIBERATE CORRECTION of another PR's pending note (never `skip-changeset`). The seat's ACCEPT confirms each changed sentence.

Nits sent along: N1 (the layered comment on the removed lookup), N2 (one preserved-half leg per name at the doors), N3 (the `/published` mixed-holder guard: residue card if needed).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ce8d6e76ff3500b36b3cfc63d243027817c0540f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.bundle-without-canonical-member-bare-read-absent.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.shipped-base-dependent-canonical-row-not-published.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-bundle-members.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-write-gates.ts, .changeset/34682-bundle-member-selector.md
Security-touching: no

Read for this record: card #34682 (body and all 8 comments), PR #34910 (body, file list, comments, the net diff `origin/main...ce8d6e76ff`), the check-runs on the head, and the cited code at the head with `git show` (no checkout, nothing built or run). The remainder of the diff (the five test files) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the tests were read to learn which arrangements are pinned, not reviewed.

Governing text: `BUNDLE_MEMBER_SELECTOR_DESCRIPTION` (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`): "Absent, the canonical member (`en-US` for `email_template`), which is what a bare-name read answers; naming the canonical value is the same request. […] A well-formed member with nothing stored or shipped answers as that door answers an absent item." Rulings: claim revision 6953406266 (the `(narrowing)` arm), seat ruling on S1 exit (a) (PR comment 6963435977).

Earlier L2 round (S1, S2, N1, N2), state on this head:

- S1: closed. `exactQualifierItem` asks the admitted holder with `bundleMemberDiscriminator(request.type, member)`, so a read naming no member asks for the canonical member; a type with no members still passes `undefined`. All five call sites (plain read: the preview draft, the strict draft, the code step; layered read: code, overlay, draft) were read: three compare the result to the item in hand, so the move changes none of them; the two code-step sites are the fix.
- S2: closed. The new entry names three arrangements, the exact address and the disabled-holder re-address included; the sibling's false sentence is corrected.
- N1: closed. The layered comment at the removed lookup states the present rule only.
- N2: closed. The runtime pin has a preserved `?member=fr-FR` leg per name.
- N3 (the `/published` mixed-holder guard) was sent as a residue-card option and is not part of this head; it stays the seat's.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`readMetaItem` (plain read, execution read): the code layers' answer is kept only at the addressed member, the canonical one when none is named** (`wantedMember !== undefined` where `main` tested `member !== undefined`). Right. It is the selector sentence. Every source the code step can take was read: the artifact lookup (asked at `wantedMember`), the package-scoped resolver's answer, the package slot, `getItem` and its plural retry all pass through the one filter; the service copy and the stored row were already read at the wanted member.
- **`getMetaItemLayered`: the same filter (`namedMemberOnly`), and the member-less artifact lookup of #34644 removed.** Right for a bundled type: that lookup was the producer of "another member as the code layer". `/layers` naming no member now equals `/layers?member=en-US`. This reverses a TO that 18.6.0 published, and the changeset says so, quoting it. See S3 for what the removal also moves.
- **`registryMemberServedAt`: naming no member, the fallback is the base's own canonical member, never its first shipped member.** Right.
- **`exactQualifierItem`: another package's item is replaced by the holder's item at the addressed member.** Right (S1).
- **Public surface.** No zod schema, export, key, stored shape or route moves. `packages/spec` gains one semantic entry id (`bundle-without-canonical-member-bare-read-absent`) in step 18 and one changed `surface` string on a sibling entry; both project into the generated registry, `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide at publish. The accept-set of every request is unchanged (a selector on a type with no members is still 400); what moves is served answers: 200 to 404 (execution: item to `null`) for a read naming no member at an address that holds no canonical member.
- **Unchanged, as declared:** a named member (the changed conditions are equal when a member is named), `/published`, and a bundle whose canonical member is shipped. Two exceptions to "exactly as before" are S3.
- **Gate verdicts on the head:** 60 check-runs `success`, 13 `skipped`, none failed or pending. `Check Changeset`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Test Core` (10 shards), `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Spec property liveness` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are among the successes.

### ② Semver level

Right. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` and `@objectstack/spec: patch`: `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct (nothing a metadata author can write moves), and AGENTS.md Post-Task 3 gives `none` a `patch` and has a breaking non-protocol change "ship `patch` and keep its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". Both packages are moved by the diff; `objectql` and `runtime` change in tests only and publish nothing. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is line-initial in the PR body and the changeset, the title carries `!`, the changeset has the BREAKING banner, a Migration line and exactly one marker (`adr-0087: registered bundle-without-canonical-member-bare-read-absent`), and the id matches the entry. The two quoted 18.6.0 statements match `packages/metadata-protocol/CHANGELOG.md` on `main` word for word.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev open question (round 0): does the change take the `(narrowing)` arm?** Answered by the seat (6953406266, option A), and I agree: a public read moves from 200 to 404, the same class PR #34644 registered.
- **Dev deviation 3 / the question put to this review: is amending the released sibling entry right?** Yes, in this PR.
  - A semantic entry is not a release note. It is a structured TODO of the major's step (`MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18].semantic`), handed whole to an upgrader crossing into 18 at whatever 18.x is current. Left alone, the sibling would tell that upgrader "the plain read … and the execution read do not move" beside a new entry that moves them: two entries of one step contradicting each other.
  - No rule forbids it. AGENTS.md makes `content/docs/releases/` and `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` release-owned, and neither is touched: the released 34441 changeset stays deleted and the 18.6.0 CHANGELOG text stands. `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md` forbids editing `registry.ts` and regenerating the projections, not editing an entry, and its third rule expects "two cards editing the same entry". ADR-0087's "a superseded decision is still a record" (Prime Directive 13) is about ADR decisions; the decision of #34441 (the `/published` narrowing, id, replacement, reason, acceptance criterion) is untouched.
  - The record of what 18.6.0 said is kept where it belongs: this PR's changeset quotes both reversed statements, and the amended sentence itself says what was served before.
  - Precedent: `17.storage-service-list-retired.ts` was amended in place. It kept its original paragraph and added a dated `AMENDED` note; here the sentence is replaced. See N4.
- **Dev deviation: commit 538121f231 pushed under an overlap-check exit 1.** Process, the lane seat's; the head reviewed here was pushed after a clean check and the checks on it are green.
- **Dev out-of-scope observation: the registry's bare-name read still answers a bundle with no canonical member with its first member.** Accepted as the registry's documented contract, but the PR's claim that the answer "reaches no door" does not hold at one more site: S4.
- **Dev out-of-scope observation: `/published` answers 404 for an item only code ships.** Agreed: not the member selector's, pinned as the baseline.
- **SQL push-down.** No finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; every changed line filters an item already in hand or passes a member to an existing registry read.

### ④ Design judgment

**`18.bundle-without-canonical-member-bare-read-absent.ts` (hits).** Holds against the code. Arrangement (1): the wanted-member filter in both reads, before and after a restart. Arrangement (2): naming no package, the resolver's first-member answer is dropped by the filter, and after a restart the dependent's hydrated canonical row is refused by `registryMemberServedAt` (the base ships no canonical member). Arrangement (3): `exactQualifierItem`. "`?member=CANONICAL`, a named non-canonical member and `/published` do not move" is true of the tree. `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` agree with the selector sentence, and "no relevance question" is right (the move turns on what holders ship and store). The entry does not name the `/layers` code-layer move of S3.

**`18.shipped-base-dependent-canonical-row-not-published.ts` (hits).** The amended sentence is true of the tree, and the rest of the entry still holds (`?package=DEPENDENT&member=CANONICAL` serves the row). Amending it here is right (③).

**`protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`.** Agrees with the contract. The comment block now says what the code does.

**`protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts`.** Agrees for a bundled type. The orphan guard comment is accurate: with the code layer the canonical member's alone, `isWantedMember(code)` holds by construction and the guard is kept.

**`protocol-write-gates.ts`.** Agrees. N5.

**`protocol-bundle-members.ts`.** The new docblock sentence "so it reaches no door" is not yet true: S4.

**`protocol-exact-qualifier.ts`.** The changed hunk agrees (S1 closed). The unchanged admission step in the same file still departs from the sentence: S4.

**Changeset.** The banner, the three arrangements, the restart sentence and the migration line agree with the code. One sentence overstates: S3.

S3 (should-fix) — the declaration says "served exactly as before" for two answers the diff moves. Read from the tree, not run.

- (a) The changeset says "A bundle that ships or stores its canonical member is served exactly as before." Take a bundle whose canonical member is stored (a package-less or a pair's `en-US` row) over a package that ships only `fr-FR`. On `main`, `/layers` naming no member reports `code` = the package's `fr-FR` body: before hydration `getItem` naming no member answers its first tier entry, and after it the removed lookup did. On this head `code` is `null`, as `/layers?member=en-US` already answered. Status and `effective` do not move, but `code` does, and so does whatever the envelope derives from `code ?? overlay`. The new answer is the right one; it is not declared, and neither the changeset nor the entry names it. No pin in the diff holds this arrangement at the doors (the runtime pin has shipped-both and stored-both names, not shipped-`fr-FR` with a stored `en-US`).
- (b) The changeset says "so is every type with no members", and the PR body says removing the lookup "changes nothing for such a type". The removed lookup ran for every type when `code` was still `null` and no member was named. For a type the exact qualifier does not judge (a `doc`), at `?package=X` where X holds nothing of the name and the only holder is a disabled package, `registryAnswerAtAddress` answers nothing (it names no disabled holder), and on `main` the removed lookup then put that disabled package's artifact back as the `code` layer of `/layers?package=X`. On this head it is `null`. Again the new answer is the right one (ruling 6917064203; a disabled package holds no name), and I am less sure of this one than of (a): whether the artifact lookup reaches a disabled package's slot in a live stack is not something I could confirm by reading.
- Fix: state both in the changeset (and (a) in the entry's `surface`, since a `/layers` caller is its reader), or pin that they do not move. A pin of (a) at the doors is worth having either way.
